newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz non-life insurance sees satisfactory 1996.
newsitem.headline: Allianz non-life insurance sees satisfactory 1996.

text.p: The non-life insurance unit of German insurer Allianz AG said on Thursday it expects satisfactory profits this year, despite falling German premium revenues in the first nine months.

Reiner Hagemann, management board chairman of Allianz's domestic non-life insurance group, said in a statement that German non-life premium revenues totalled 14.1 billion marks ($9.4 billion) to the end of September, down 1.2 percent from a year ago. ($ = 1.501 German Marks)

"New business continues to develop satisfactorily," he said, adding that new policies grew 6.2 percent to 1.5 million during the same period. "But in light of the weak domestic economy, premium revenues as a whole are declining."
"On condition that the extraordinarily good development in damage coverage continues to the end of the year, Allianz expects generally satisfactory results in its non-life business in 1996," he said.
Premium revenues in car insurance were down 4.5 percent, while revenues in all other areas combined rose 1.9 percent.
Payments resulting from damages were below the average of the previous year. He noted in particular a decline in coverage for substantial damages of 250,000 marks or more.
Capital investments of Allianz's non-life unit at the end of September were 28.6 billion marks, up 2.1 billion marks.
Profits from capital investments were 1.3 billion marks, or 34 million marks higher than the year before.
